standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, the lemma characterising perfect complexes over Noetherian rings through the finite type and boundedness properties

core_obligations: Trivialise on an etale covering (proof lines 13859-13865): choose a covering {U_i -> X} over which K becomes constant, i.e. K|U_i is isomorphic to the constant complex underline M_i^bullet for finite complexes of finite Lambda-modules M_i^bullet, by the local constancy description.

Separate the isomorphism classes (proof lines 13866-13872): if M_i^bullet is not isomorphic to M_j^bullet in D(Lambda) then U_i x_X U_j is empty; grouping the indices by isomorphism class, the subsets U_{M^bullet} = union of the images Im(U_i -> X) are open because etale morphisms are open, and X is their disjoint union.

Conclude by connectedness and perfectness (proof lines 13873-13878): connectedness of X leaves exactly one nonempty U_{M^bullet}, so K is constant on the chosen covering over a single M^bullet, and since K lies in the constructible finite type category the perfectness criterion makes M^bullet a perfect complex of Lambda-modules, whence it may be taken to be a finite complex of finite projective modules.
proof_roadmap: Trivialise K on an etale covering and record the finite complexes of finite modules appearing.
Group the covering by the derived isomorphism class of the local model and use openness of etale morphisms to get a disjoint open decomposition.
Use connectedness to single out one model and perfectness to make it a finite complex of finite projective modules.
difficulty_reason: The lemma makes a locally constant constructible complex on a connected scheme globally constant on an etale covering, over a finite complex of finite projective modules (statement lines 13849-13856). The proof (proof lines 13858-13878) trivialises the complex on an etale covering, separates the covering into the disjoint open pieces indexed by the isomorphism class of the local model — using that etale morphisms are open and that U_i x_X U_j is empty for non-isomorphic models — and then uses connectedness together with the perfectness criterion to replace the surviving model by a finite complex of finite projective modules. H2: the same grouping argument as for locally constant sheaves, with one extra perfectness input.
